exposure: Women who had a successful trial of labor after myomectomy (TOLAM)
Women who had an elective caesarean section (ELCS)
outcome: Patient satisfaction with mode of birth
Patient preference for mode of birth in future pregnancies
cohort: Women who had an open or laparoscopic myomectomy followed by a pregnancy within 3 maternity units in a single NHS trust in the UK over a 5-year period
finding: While 95% of women were satisfied with their mode of birth, 80% would prefer vaginal birth in a future pregnancy, highlighting a discrepancy between experienced and preferred mode of birth in this population.
mod_finding: While 95% of women who had either a trial of labor after myomectomy (TOLAM) or an elective cesarean section (ELCS) were satisfied with their mode of birth, 80% expressed a preference for vaginal birth in future pregnancies.
